levels.title: Real or unreal?
levels.full: Overview of Basic Verb Forms Used in Conditional Sentences

items.title: Real: it can happen
lines: if + present. Result: present (habit) or will (future).

items.title: Unreal: only imagine it
lines: Now: if + past, would. Past: if + had + participle, would have.

items.text: If I lived underwater, I would see colorful marine life every day.
If I had more money right now, I ___ lend you some.

items.title: The four patterns
lines: Tap to hear each one.
chips: If I have enough time, I watch TV every evening.
If I have enough time, I will watch TV later on tonight.
If I had enough time, I would watch TV now.
If I had had enough time, I would have watched TV yesterday.

items.text: “If you had studied yesterday, you ___ well on the test.”

lines: Real: if + present → present / will.
Unreal now: if + past → would. Unreal past: if + had + participle → would have + participle.

examples.text: If I have enough time, I will watch TV later on tonight.
If I had enough time, I would watch TV now.
If I had had enough time, I would have watched TV yesterday.

levels.title: If it rains…
levels.full: Expressing Real Conditions in the Present or Future

items.title: if + present
lines: Never will in the if-clause.
chips: If I don't eat breakfast, I always get hungry during class. (habit)
If I don't eat breakfast tomorrow morning, I will get hungry during class. (future)

items.text: If the baby wakes up in the middle of the night, she cries. This is…

items.title: Facts: present or will
lines: Both are fine for general truths.
chips: Water freezes if the temperature reaches 0°C.
Water will freeze if the temperature reaches 0°C.

items.title: Other results
lines: Modals and imperatives work too.
chips: If it rains, we should stay home.
If it rains, I might decide to stay home.
If it rains, we can't go.
If anyone calls, please take a message.

items.title: if + should = less sure
lines: Almost the same meaning.
chips: If anyone should call, please take a message.
If the plane should take off late, we'll miss our connecting flight.

items.text: If I find out the answer, I ___ you know.
items.why: One time in the future → will.

lines: if + simple present → present (habit / fact) or will (future).
The result can also be a modal or an imperative. if + should = a little less sure.

examples.text: If I don't eat breakfast, I always get hungry during class.
If it rains, we should stay home.
If anyone should call, please take a message.

talk.title: Superstitions
talk.task: What happens if you see a black cat? Walk under a ladder? Tell Claude what people believe.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me one question at a time about superstitions: What may happen on Friday the 13th? What happens if you walk under a ladder? if you see a black cat? if you find a four-leaf clover? if you break a mirror? What superstitions do people have in your country? I answer with if + simple present, will/may (If you break a mirror, you will have seven years of bad luck.). Check that I never use will in the if-clause.

levels.title: If I were you…

items.title: Imagine it now
lines: if + simple past, would + verb. It is NOT true.

items.title: were for everyone
lines: I, he, she, it → were.
chips: If I were you, I would accept their invitation.

talk.title: What would you do?
talk.task: If you were given a million dollars, what would you do? Claude asks fun “what if” questions.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me one imaginary question at a time: If you had the choice of any job in the world, what would it be? If someone famous invited you to dinner, who would you want it to be? If you were given a million dollars, what would you do with it? If you were lost on a desert island with only three items, what would they be? If you spoke five languages fluently, which ones would they be? I answer with would (If I had the choice, I would be ...). Check: simple past (were) in the if-clause, would + simple verb in the result.

talk.title: If I had known…
talk.task: Claude says: “I didn't know it was your birthday.” You answer: “If I had known…”
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. levels.title: If it weren't raining…
levels.full: Using Progressive Verb Forms in Conditional Sentences

items.title: In progress? Keep -ing
lines: Now: were + -ing. Past: had been + -ing.
chips: It is raining right now, so I will not go for a walk. → If it were not raining right now, I would go for a walk.
It was raining yesterday, so I did not go for a walk. → If it had not been raining, I would have gone for a walk.

items.text: I'm working. If I ___ working, I would be at home.
The copy machine wasn't working. If it ___ working, we would have finished our presentation.

items.title: Flip the fact
lines: Positive fact → negative if. Negative fact → positive if.
chips: You aren't wearing a coat, so you're cold. → If you were wearing a coat, you wouldn't be cold.

items.text: YOKO: “If I weren't painting my apartment, I would go to a movie.” Is Yoko painting now?

lines: Now: if + were (not) + -ing → would.
Past: if + had (not) been + -ing → would have.

talk.title: Suppose…

What if you were the guest? / Suppose there were a fire in your home and you had time to save only one thing. / John was cheating during an exam. Suppose you were the teacher and you saw him.
